newsitem.title: FRANCE: Guerrilla Carlos won't talk without his belt on.
newsitem.headline: Guerrilla Carlos won't talk without his belt on.

text.p: British investigators flew to Paris on Friday to question "Carlos the Jackal", but the guerrilla mastermind refused to talk because prison guards had removed his belt, his lawyer said.
Lawyer Frederic Pariente said Carlos refused to be taken from his Paris prison cell without his belt.
Paramilitary gendarmes took him by force to the office of investigating magistrate Jean-Louis Bruguiere, but he stayed silent and the questioning was postponed.
Prison guards routinely take belts and shoelaces away from inmates to prevent possible suicide by hanging.

Three Scotland Yard investigators had wanted to question Carlos, whose real name is Illich Ramirez Sanchez, over the 1977 attempted murder in London of Joseph Edward Sieff, chairman of Marks and Spencer department stores.
Venezuelan-born Carlos was spirited to Paris from Sudan in 1994 and is awaiting trial on various charges of bombing and murder.
He was given a suspended 10 days in solitary confinement earlier this month after calling a guard, "You wildebeest, you!".

French police accuse Carlos of killing 83 people in a series of attacks in Europe and the Middle East. The boldest incident with which he was linked was the kidnapping of 11 OPEC oil ministers in Vienna in 1975.
